generation.keys: Use distinct consecutive integer primary keys; count keys among integer fields. Generate relationship keys from each scenario's relationship.

strings.rounding: lower bound ceiling; upper bound floor

repetition.reset: Regenerate equivalent input and history; reset target to the case initial state and initialize independent CDC positions and operator state.
repetition.database_process: Reuse within the batch by default; record cache and warm-up conditions.
repetition.aggregation: Keep each raw result and completion status; report medians and variation for eligible repeats.

single-node-op.mongodb: shared test replica set with isolated source and target databases

single-node-op-dedicated-target.mongodb: independent target instance for both paired arms when target-write isolation requires it

incremental.rounding: Floor each operation quota and allocate the remaining units by descending fractional remainder, with insert, update, delete as the tie order.

selection.insert: Take unique keys from a range disjoint from the initial keys.
selection.update: Pair with inserts first, after the insert on the same stream. Pick excess update keys uniformly without replacement from eligible initial keys.
selection.delete: Pick uniformly without replacement from initial keys, excluding keys selected for an independent update.
selection.order: Seed the interleaving, preserve each insert-update dependency, keep warm-up keys separate, and preserve per-stream boundaries.

incremental.update_rounding: Round to nearest with ties up and a minimum of one field.
incremental.update: Keep primary and relationship keys and required filter fields unchanged. Make actual value changes, including an observable output field when propagation is expected.

snapshot.start: Start the isolated snapshot after input and environment preparation.
snapshot.finish: Both all inputs are consumed and all expected target writes or consumptions are acknowledged. Take the later boundary.
snapshot.unit: source rows and case-defined target units

live-latency.start: Attribute each eligible unit to the source connector event time in the half-open scoring window.
live-latency.finish: Use the actual acknowledgements for all expected target writes of that unit, including in-window units completed during bounded drain.
live-latency.unit: case-defined source event or acknowledged group

backlog-throughput.start: Start isolated catch-up after prewriting the fixed batch and recording each input boundary.
backlog-throughput.finish: Take the later time of all streams reaching their final positions and all expected writes obtaining target acknowledgement.
backlog-throughput.unit: actual source events and case-defined target units
metrics: input events and bytes per second
output units and bytes per second

eligibility.timeout_or_missing_boundary: Keep partial evidence and mark the sample incomplete. Check target contents independently of measurement eligibility.
eligibility.comparison: Bind runtime, code, connector lock, machine, configuration, case version and effective recipe. Keep unsupported byte, resource and timing readings missing.
